description:
A beautiful interactive website featuring:

Interactive Moon and Mars map showing NASA equipment left behind.

Clickable equipment with its history, mission, discoveries and current status.

AI-generated educational storytelling.

Timeline from the Apollo era to modern Mars exploration.

Interactive 3D-style visual presentation.

A quiz where visitors test their space knowledge.

Why I like it:

It is explicitly classified as Beginner/Youth friendly in the challenge listings.
summary:
What we built and how it works
LUNAR LEGACY is an interactive web atlas that brings the story of human hardware on the Moon and Mars to life for students, educators, and space fans. Instead of buried spreadsheets, users explore dual-world maps, filter missions by era (from 1959 Luna probes and Apollo landers to Perseverance, Chandrayaan-3, and SLIM), and click any site to view real coordinates, mass, science breakthroughs, and Artemis heritage safety zones (500 m – 2 km).

Why it matters & Challenge alignment
Built for "Abandoned but not Forgotten," our project turns 104+ sites and 200+ tons of off-world hardware into an engaging STEM storytelling tool. With Artemis and global landers returning soon, dust plumes and rover traffic put historic sites at risk. Making this data visual helps inspire young learners while highlighting international spaceflight heritage.

Data & Tech Stack
We combined open datasets from NASA (LROC QuickMap, HiRISE, Planetary Data System, NSSDCA) and Space Agency Partners (ESA, JAXA, and ISRO mission archives) to verify global coordinates. Built with lightweight HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript, the app runs smoothly on school laptops and phones with zero backend setup, hosted on GitHub Pages.
details:
What It Does & How It Works LUNAR LEGACY is an interactive off-world heritage atlas and mission-control web application that maps, catalogs, and visualizes humanity's historic spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments across the Moon and Mars. Users can toggle between high-resolution lunar and Martian coordinate maps, filter sites by chronological spaceflight era (from 1959 Luna impactors and Apollo landing sites to modern Mars rovers and Artemis-era missions), inspect detailed telemetry dossiers (exact latitude/longitude coordinates, landing dates, hardware mass, mission status, and orbital verification notes), and visualize recommended heritage protection buffer zones around historic sites.

Benefits & Intended Impact Since 1959, humanity has left behind more than 104 documented sites and over 200 metric tons of historic hardware on the Moon and Mars. As lunar and Martian exploration accelerates under the Artemis program and commercial lander missions, these irreplaceable milestones of human achievement face growing risks from rocket plume blast ejecta, dust abrasion, and rover traffic. LUNAR LEGACY makes fragmented planetary archives intuitive and accessible for mission planners, researchers, educators, and students—helping raise awareness for off-world heritage preservation while inspiring the next generation of space explorers.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), responsive interactive SVG/Canvas planetary coordinate mapping, and custom telemetry UI components.
  • Typography & Styling: Google Fonts (Syne, Space Grotesk, and JetBrains Mono) for high-contrast mission-control readability.
  • Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and GitHub Pages for zero-backend, instant browser accessibility across desktop and mobile devices.

Creativity & Design Considerations Rather than presenting planetary coordinates in static spreadsheets or dense technical PDFs, we designed LUNAR LEGACY as a dual-world interactive "Mission Control" atlas that connects historical storytelling with real orbital science. Key considerations included zero-install browser performance, accurate planetary coordinate projection, clear visual indicators for Artemis safety exclusion zones (500 m – 2 km), and strict adherence to open NASA data provenance.
